claims.text: Basic labs for any suspected ingestion: CMP; acetaminophen, salicylate and ethanol levels; lactate and blood gas; urinalysis; urine toxicology screen.
claims.quote: The basic laboratory evaluation of a patient with suspected use of a xenobiotic is typically performed, including: complete metabolic profile; serum acetaminophen (paracetamol), salicylate, and ethanol concentrations; serum lactate and blood gas; urinalysis; and urine toxicology screen.

claims.text: Alcohol: fingerstick glucose to rule out hypoglycemia, and sometimes a BAC.
claims.quote: Exceptions include fingerstick glucose to rule out hypoglycemia and sometimes tests to determine BAC.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: A low BAC with altered mental status speeds the search for another cause.
claims.quote: However, finding a low BAC in patients who have altered mental status is helpful because it expedites the search for an alternate cause.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: A high BAC doesn't explain obtundation after minor trauma; look for intracranial injury.
claims.quote: Clinicians should not assume that a high BAC in patients with apparently minor trauma accounts for their obtundation, which may be due to intracranial injury or other abnormalities.
claims.locator: Diagnosis of Alcohol Toxicity and Withdrawal

claims.text: Amphetamines, ECG: sinus tachycardia or another tachydysrhythmia; with rhabdomyolysis, peaked T waves or VT from hyperkalemia.
claims.quote: An ECG may show a tachydysrhythmia, such as sinus tachycardia or, in cases with rhabdomyolysis, peaked T waves or ventricular tachycardia from hyperkalemia.

claims.text: Urine amphetamine immunoassay: false positives are frequent (eg, ibuprofen, naproxen, doxylamine); methylphenidate does not cross-react.
claims.quote: The urine immunoassay tests for an epitope that amphetamine shares with its derivatives and many other substances, including ibuprofen , naproxen , and doxylamine . The lack of structural specificity of this immunoassay frequently leads to false-positive results or cross-reactions. However, methylphenidate (commonly used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) does not cross-react to produce a false positive in amphetamine testing.

claims.text: Cocaine: the metabolite benzoylecgonine is on most routine urine drug screens.
claims.quote: The cocaine metabolite, benzoylecgonine, is part of most routine urine drug screening tests

claims.text: Cocaine chest pain: serial ECGs, cardiac markers and chest x-ray; for possible aortic dissection, ECG, chest x-ray and chest CT.
claims.quote: Cocaine -related chest pain is evaluated in the same manner as for any patient with potential myocardial ischemia (serial ECG, serum cardiac markers and chest radiograph) or aortic dissection (ECG, chest radiograph and chest CT).
